facts.claim: Linear's hosted MCP server (streamable HTTP, primary) is at /mcp
The MCP host and the OAuth issuer, authorize, token and register endpoints are all on mcp.linear.app
facts.evidence: Discovery document: issuer https://mcp.linear.app, authorization/token/registration endpoints on the same host; docs page names the same host.

facts.claim: Docs name OAuth scopes read (read-only) and default read-write on /mcp; discovery lists read, write, openid, email; template leaves scopes empty so the server decides
facts.evidence: Protected-resource document: scopes_supported [read, write]; docs: requesting only the read scope limits to read-only.

facts.claim: Dynamic client registration is offered, so no OAuth app has to be created first (mcp-oauth, client_registration auto)
facts.evidence: registration_endpoint https://mcp.linear.app/register; docs: Interactive OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration.

facts.claim: A Linear API key or OAuth access token can be sent as a bearer Authorization header instead of the browser sign-in
facts.evidence: Bearer token in the Authorization header (OAuth access token or API key).

facts.claim: https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly exposes only read tools; https://mcp.linear.app/sse is the deprecated SSE fallback
facts.evidence: Read-only endpoint and deprecated SSE fallback are listed on the docs page.

facts.claim: Linear's 2025 changelog announced the server at /sse (since superseded by /mcp)
facts.evidence: Server URL given there is https://mcp.linear.app/sse.

choices.because: Docs name browser OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and the discovery document advertises a registration endpoint, so nothing must be created first; hosted beats running a local package.
Docs give no required scope; the server decides (read-write by default, read scope narrows to read-only).
Linear's docs name no tools, so none could be quoted from the vendor.

open: Linear's docs name no tool names; no smoke op or tool-based consent list could be sourced (tool names change at runtime via tools/list).
The /mcp path itself rests on one vendor page (the discovery documents confirm the host, not the path).
The docs state no plan requirement for MCP; admin requirements are mentioned only for Okta-managed authorization.
Whether an API key or token as bearer is accepted was read on one page and not tested (no requests to the MCP endpoint allowed).
The 2025 changelog gives /sse, the docs page gives /mcp; the docs page is current and treats /sse as deprecated.
